title: The Great Migration
subtitle: How movement shaped Murle settlement patterns
body: Long journeys across changing landscapes are a recurring theme in Murle oral history. Communities moved in response to drought, conflict, and the search for better grazing land, gradually settling in the areas of Jonglei and Boma that many Murle call home today.

These migrations were rarely simple relocations. They involved negotiation with neighboring communities, the founding of new settlements, and the adaptation of traditions to new environments while preserving the core of Murle identity.

Elders often point to specific rivers, hills, and landmarks as waypoints in these journeys, each carrying its own story. Recording these landmarks and the memories attached to them is an ongoing act of cultural preservation.
Understanding this history helps explain the geography of Murle communities today, and the deep attachment many still feel to particular rivers and plains.
